summary: A declarative, schema-bound cross-field validation engine: JSON rules (when/then path+op pairs) are compiled to an interpreted AST, cached per schema in a GenServer, and evaluated against documents at mutate, live, and export time, emitting structured violations for the v2 error envelope.

intentions.title: Enforce domain-specific cross-field business rules without code changes
intentions.evidence: rules.ex compiles JSON rule maps (e.g. 'isbn-required when format==epub') into Rule structs; evaluator.ex runs them at runtime — schema authors declare rules in data, not Elixir code (Decision D7 in rule.ex: no Code.eval_*)

intentions.title: Gate content mutations, live previews, and ONIX exports at different validation checkpoints
intentions.evidence: evaluator.ex tag filtering (:live, :mutate, :export) — a rule fires only for the tagged operation; rules.ex parses tag lists from JSON into a MapSet; downstream WI2/WI3/WI4 comments name the concrete consumers

intentions.title: Keep the hot validation path allocation-cheap via memoisation and a compiled AST
intentions.evidence: evaluator.ex per-pass cache keyed by {op, value, args} short-circuits repeated checker calls on array docs; rules.ex deliberately avoids ETS (tiny dataset, rare writes) and returns a pre-compiled list on GenServer.call

intentions.title: Make validation extensible to external checkers without touching core ops
intentions.evidence: ops.ex {:matches, name} clause delegates to Barkpark.Validation.Registry.find/1 → mod.check/2; rules.ex maps 'matches:isbn13' op strings to {:matches, 'isbn13'} tuples — WI3 registers codelist_ref this way

intentions.title: Surface violations with precise, wildcard-expanded JSON-Pointer paths for UI error mapping
intentions.evidence: path.ex resolves /items/*/tags/* to concrete paths like /items/2/tags/0, substituting array indices; evaluator.ex build_violation/2 puts the concrete path in the violation map consumed by WI2's error envelope serializer
